the cytosolic class P1, Mu and Alpha GSTs are the major GST isoenzymes in human liver and that the class P1 and Alpha GSTs were found to be increased in the plasma of patients with urinary and renal cancer.
the ELISAS are suitable for analyzing cytosolic GST phenotypes in normal and tumor cells, and in monitoring plasma GST levels in patients with urinary bladder and renal cancer.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel immunoassay system for the analysis of cytosolic glutatathione transferase (GST).
the application of the GST isoenzymes in cancer diagnosis.

the analysis of the GST profiles in normal and tumor cells, with the development of isoenzyme-specific immunoassays and with the monitoring of plasma GST levels in patients with urinary bladder and renal cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GST M1-2 and GST P1 are the most sensitive markers of exposure to carcinogens, and that the GST A1-2 is a more specific indicator of the risk of lung cancer.
the plasma GST profile of cancer patients is a complex mixture of GSTs of various origins.
the GST P1- isoenzyme is the most important one to consider for the diagnosis and monitoring of urinary bladder cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plasma GST levels are increased in cancer patients, and the increases are not due to the tumor per se but are caused by the disease process itself.
the GSTs are a family of isozymes that can be separated by isoelectric focusing and that they are expressed at different levels in different tissues and in tumor cells.

we have developed sensitive and accurate ELISA methods for the quantification of GSTs in biological samples and applied the methods to establish the GST phenotypes of tumor cells and to monitor the GST levels in the plasma of cancer patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ELISAS can be used for monitoring GSTs in cancer cells, as well as in plasma of cancer patients, and that GST M1-2, M1-3, M1-4 and P1-1 are the most promising candidates for clinical studies.
the GST profile of tumor cells is a valuable marker for tumor diagnosis and that the plasma levels of GST M1- 1 and P1-1 can be used for the monitoring of cancer patients.
the GSTs are useful markers for monitoring cancer patients and for identifying the origin of a primary tumor.
